name: Us Then vs Us Now
why_it_works: Comparing yourself to your own past is the only comparison that never insults anyone. Showing the rough first version earns sympathy, the glow-up proves growth, and long-time fans feel ownership because they were there for the 'then'.

hook.pattern: Open on your own embarrassing first version and own it before anyone can laugh.
examples: This was our first {{first_thing}}. Yes, really.
If you liked us back then, you have to see this.

variables.name: then_detail
variables.description: An honest detail about the rough start
variables.example: one mic, a borrowed laptop, 14 streams

variables.name: now_detail
variables.example: a full band in a real studio

variables.name: what_stayed
variables.example: every song still starts on the same cheap guitar

variables.name: offer
variables.example: New single out Friday, pre-save now

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 photo styled as an old phone snapshot from {{then_year}}: grainy, slightly overexposed, cramped room with makeshift setup, honest and charming, faded colors
Vertical grainy photo of a makeshift early setup for {{brand}}, borrowed gear, tangled cables, warm lamp light, documentary feel
Vertical cinematic slow push-in on {{now_detail}} for {{brand}}, professional lighting, crisp modern color grade, confident energy, no text

beats.on_screen_text: If you were here then, thank you.

visual.prompt: Vertical warm photo of a small crowd or community of supporters around {{brand}}, candid smiles, golden light, faces softly blurred

cta: Be here for the next chapter: {{offer}}.

craft.notes: The 'then' must be genuinely rough; a fake-humble start reads as a flex. The 'what stayed' beat is the emotional anchor: it tells fans the growth didn't cost you your identity. Ask in the caption for people to say when they found you.

do_not: Stage a fake 'then' photo; use real early material or recreate it honestly and say so
Mock your earlier self so hard that early fans feel mocked too
Use samples of other artists' songs in the 'then' audio
